Moderate12_GiltsAtYield.label: Moderate12_GiltsAtYield
Moderate12_GiltsAtYield.description: Identical to the headline Moderate-12% problem except that the expected-return vector fed to the optimiser uses the redemption yield (yield to maturity) for both individual gilts in place of the 50/50 historical/yield blend.
Moderate12_GiltsAtYield.rationale: For a gilt held to maturity the forward return is its redemption yield. The 5-year sample mean is dominated by the 2021-2023 repricing from ~1% to ~5.3% yields, which has already happened and cannot repeat from today's level, so blending it into the forward estimate double-counts a past capital loss. See the gilt bullet in data/analysis_results.json -> limitations.
Moderate12_GiltsAtYield.expected_return_input_note: blend, with T36N and T56 at redemption yield

Moderate12_Diversified.label: Moderate12_Diversified
Moderate12_Diversified.description: The headline problem with the per-asset concentration caps tightened: single fund line (equity ETF, bond ETF, commodity ETC, gilt, trend fund) 20% -> 10%, single stock 5% -> 4%. Group constraints and all three expected-return estimates unchanged.
Moderate12_Diversified.rationale: The headline core holds 17.1% in one line (SMGB.L, VanEck Semiconductor UCITS ETF) which contributes about 37% of its ex-ante Ledoit-Wolf variance. This variant prices the cost, in expected return, of forcing that concentration down.

limitations: Educational analysis, not personalised advice; every figure is a model output.

Both variants are single-change sensitivities on one already noisy problem. A mean-variance optimiser maximises estimation error (Michaud 1989), so the weight differences below are larger than the confidence one should attach to them.

Variant A replaces the two gilts' blended mu with their redemption yield but leaves every other line (including the HY/EM credit ETFs and IBTM.L, which already use a yield-based estimate #2) on the 50/50 blend, so it is a sensitivity, not a coherent all-forward-looking expected-return vector.

A gilt's redemption yield is the forward return only if it is HELD TO MATURITY and coupons are reinvested at that yield; the covariance matrix still uses the ETF-proxy history (IGLT.L for T36N, GLTL.L for T56), whose duration and volatility are those of a rolling fund, not of a single bond pulling to par.
Variant B's 10% single-fund cap is applied to every fund bucket including the trend fund DBMG.L, whose separate 15% group limit is left in place but is no longer binding.

The 12% target is the ex-ante Ledoit-Wolf volatility of the optimised 97.5%; adding the 2.5% SPCX policy weight at its 67-bar pairwise covariance raises the full-core figure (reported alongside as ex_ante_vol_full_core_incl_spcx).
Backtests are 5 years of monthly rebalancing with no dealing costs, no stamp duty, no FX charge and no spread; they apply the variant weights to past returns and are not a track record.
Beta/beta+/beta- are as-held sums including SPCX at its own 67-bar betas, which are not estimates; the _excl_spcx fields are given for every portfolio.
Turnover is one-way (0.5 x sum of absolute weight changes) against the PUBLISHED headline weights in data/weights.csv.
